We are a creative team that loves building smart and useful solutions.
Each member brings different skills — like web development, graphic design, video editing, AI and Machine Learning ,research, and content creation — which helps us turn ideas into real projects.

We enjoy exploring new technologies, improving our work, and solving problems in simple and engaging ways.
Our goal is to make complex topics easier to understand and more fun to interact with.
summary:
We built SkyBlink, a web tool that helps anyone spot moving objects in the sky, the way astronomers found Pluto
How it works: Enter coordinates (RA/Dec), pick a field of view, or open a preset target like WISE or Gaia
Press Play and flip through the frames like a short video.
Switch views: Blink, Side by side, or subtract frames (A − B) to make motion stand out.
Turn on Gaia and WISE overlays to see which objects are already known.
Save anything unmatched as a candidate and share the link.
Why it matters: SPHEREx maps the whole sky every six months, but its data is hard for most people to use. SkyBlink makes finding moving objects simple, and four interactive museum halls teach the science along the way
Current status: our prototype uses simulated pixels, with real names, positions, dates and wavelengths. Real SPHEREx data is the next step
details:
SkyBlink lets anyone watch the sky change

Enter the coordinates of WISE 0855, press Play, and the frames of that patch run like a short video. The stars stay put, and moving objects give themselves away by shifting position.

What you can do on the site:

  • Enter RA/Dec (degrees or hh:mm:ss) or open a preset target
  • Nine gallery sky patches and five challenge targets ready to open
  • Pick a field of view from 60″ to 6° and an optional date
  • Play, zoom, reset, and change speed; pick any date from May 2025 to Nov 2026 (QR3 / DR1)
  • Four views: Side by side, Blink, A − B, A + B
  • Co-add detectors and epochs for a better signal-to-noise ratio
  • Overlays: trail, target marker, Gaia, WISE, detections
  • Wavelength trap: choose a different channel for frame B and see why comparing different colors fools you
  • Everything on one TAN/WCS grid, so frames line up

How it finds movers. Align frames on one grid, subtract, find residual pairs, link them into a track, then match against Gaia and WISE. Anything left unmatched becomes a candidate. A hint unlocks only after your first click, so you try to find it yourself first.

Keep your findings. Save candidates, export a report, and copy a share link to the exact same view. Sign in to keep your candidates and favorite fields.

Learn in four museum halls. Infrared Universe, Dust and Ices, Moving Stars, Discovery. Each one is interactive and ends in the real tool.

For everyone. Arabic and English, captions, and sound.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages.

Known limit: pixels are simulated; names, positions, dates and wavelengths are real. Targets are validated from published positions and proper motions.

Next: real SPHEREx data and the Aladin Lite context map.
